title: How To Set The Tone On The First Day Of School https://smartclassroommanagement.com/2014/08/09/how-to-set-the-tone-on-the-first-day-of-school/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin argues that the first day of school is less about specific lessons or activities and more about a teacher's underlying style and demeanor, since that is what establishes classroom culture. He organizes the advice around five qualities to embody: being likable through a genuine smile, being calm to settle first-day jitters, being clear through simple, paced, and modeled instruction, being confident by speaking directly and without hedging, and being fun so students leave excited about the year ahead. He specifically pushes back on the old advice not to smile for the first two months, calling it terrible guidance. The article closes by tying these first-day behaviors to the habits that will define the rest of the year, positioning the first day as groundwork for both students and the teacher's own practice.
points: The old advice not to smile for the first two months of school is wrong; a genuine smile builds instant likability and rapport.
A calm teacher demeanor settles first-day jitters and models the peaceful environment the teacher wants to create.
Clarity—simple language, frequent pauses, and explicit modeling—should govern every first-day lesson and transition.
Confident, direct, concise speech (no hedging or repeating) builds student trust in the teacher's leadership.
First-day tone-setting isn't just for students; it also builds the teacher's own habits for the rest of the year.
quotes: It is the initial impression of your classroom, after all, that establishes its culture.
The old maxim that you shouldn’t smile the first two months of the school year is terrible advice.
A genuine smile creates instant likability, builds effortless rapport, and activates the power of reciprocation.
Your calm demeanor alone, without having to say a word, has a powerful effect on students—much more than most teachers realize.
When it comes to effective classroom management, clarity trumps all.
If you’re unsure about what to do next, if you hem and haw, repeat yourself , change your mind, think out loud, speak too much or too fast, or appear befuddled, you’ll lose your students.
The first day of school isn’t just about setting the tone for your students. It’s also about setting the tone for yourself.
